issue.title: Add testclient test for domain restricted cookies

issue.body:
As the starlette testclient uses `http://testserver` as its default `base_url`, it is obvious to set the cookie domain to `testserver` in a test setup.

This works as expected in Python 3.11, but fails in Python 3.10 and below due to a change in `http.cookiejar.DefaultCookiePolicy.set_ok_domain` (compare [3.10](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.10/Lib/http/cookiejar.py#L1047) with [3.11](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.11/Lib/http/cookiejar.py#L1046)).

For example, the following test case works fine in Python 3.11, but not in 3.10:

```py
from starlette.responses import Response
from starlette.testclient import TestClient


async def app(scope, receive, send):
    response = Response("foo")
    response.set_cookie("bar", "baz", domain="testserver")
    await response(scope, receive, send)


def test_app():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/")
    assert len(response.cookies) == 1
```

**Workaround:** Use `testserver.local` as cookie domain for testclient. This works fine in both Python 3.10 and Python 3.11.

---

**Is this a starlette issue?** I think so, somewhat, as Starlette uses `testserver` as default `base_url` - which doesn't work "as expected" if a cookie domain is set.

**What could be done about it?** Either use a different `base_url` (e.g. `testserver.local`) (this would certainly break backward compatibility in lots of tests), or just document the issue, e.g. in the [Testclient chapter](https://www.starlette.io/testclient/).
